title: Locally constant geometric fibre dimension of a smooth group space
statement: Work with schemes [def-pc-scheme] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Smoothness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite presentation means local finite presentation, quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness; quasi-compactness means that affine scheme tests have quasi-compact inverse images, and quasi-separatedness means that the diagonal is quasi-compact. Separatedness means that the representable diagonal is a closed immersion on every scheme test. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $B$ be a scheme and let $p:H\to B$ be a smooth separated group algebraic space of finite presentation. A group algebraic space has multiplication $m:H\times_BH\to H$, inverse $\iota:H\to H$ and identity $e:B\to H$ over $B$, satisfying associativity, the two unit identities and the two inverse identities; commutativity is not assumed. For $b\in B$ choose an algebraic closure $\overline{\kappa(b)}$ of its residue field [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Every geometric fibre $H_{\bar b}$ is nonempty and pure of some finite dimension $d_p(b)\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, where dimension is topological Krull dimension in the atlas topology [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension, def-a1-space-point-topology], and pure means that every irreducible component has that dimension. The function $d_p:|B|\to\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ is locally constant. For every morphism of schemes $h:B'\to B$, the base-changed group satisfies $d_{p_{B'}}=d_p\circ h$. No integrality, connectedness, properness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-space-dimension-strata] to $p$ and put $d(b)=\nu_p(e(b))$. The identity is an actual morphism over $B$. Its point map is continuous by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. Thus $d^{-1}(n)=e^{-1}(H_n)$ is open for every $n$, so $d$ is locally constant.

proof.text:
Fix $b$ and $k=\overline{\kappa(b)}$, and write $G=H_{ ar b}$. The base-change clause of [lem-sfb-smooth-space-dimension-strata] gives $
u_G(e_k)=d(b)$. For $g\in G(k)$, the maps $t_g(z)=m(g,z)$ and $t_{g^{-1}}(z)=m(\iota(g),z)$ are inverse automorphisms by associativity and the unit and inverse identities, and $t_g(e_k)=g$. An automorphism carries etale charts and their open neighbourhoods isomorphically to charts and open neighbourhoods. It therefore preserves their Krull dimensions and hence $
u_G$. Thus $
u_G(g)=d(b)$ for every rational point $g$.

source.place: groupoids.tex lemma-group-scheme-field-geometrically-irreducible, rational-point translation argument, applied directly to the group-space operations; Tag 04NS(1) for the identity under base change.

proof.text: Suppose $G_n$ is nonempty for $n\ne d(b)$. By [def-trf-algebraic-space] choose a scheme atlas of $G$ and restrict it to the nonempty open subspace $G_n$; a nonempty chart $V\to G_n$ exists. This is an etale chart of the smooth space $G$, so $V$ is smooth over $k$ by the chartwise smoothness convention. By [lem-pc-rational-points-dense], the nonempty smooth $k$-scheme $V$ has a $k$-point. Its image $g\in G_n(k)$ contradicts step 2. Consequently every point of $G$ belongs to $G_{d(b)}$.

source.place: Tag 02G1 and etale charts of the open dimension strata; latest blueprint lem-pc-rational-points-dense, using dense separable closed points. Algebraic closures are separably closed.

proof.text: The identity $e_k$ makes $G$ nonempty. Step 3 says that its dimension stratum $G_{d(b)}$ is all of $G$. The geometric-fibre clause of [lem-sfb-smooth-space-dimension-strata], applied to $H_{d(b)}\to B$, now shows that every irreducible component of $G$ has dimension $d(b)$. Thus $d=d_p$ is exactly the dimension function required in the statement, not merely a dimension at the identity.

source.place: Tag 02G2, equidimensional nonempty fibres of a fixed smooth dimension stratum, and Tag 0A4J for topological dimension.

proof.text: Steps 2--4 used only an algebraically closed field $k$ with a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}k\to B$ whose image is $b$: the base-change clause of [lem-sfb-smooth-space-dimension-strata] holds for every scheme morphism, its pure-fibre clause allows every algebraically closed field $\Omega$, and an algebraically closed field is separably closed, as [lem-pc-rational-points-dense] requires. Hence for every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and every $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to B$ with image $b$, the fibre $H\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is nonempty and pure of dimension $\nu_p(e(b))=d(b)$. In particular $d_p(b)$ does not depend on the chosen algebraic closure. Now let $h:B'\to B$ be a morphism of schemes, $p':H'=H\times_BB'\to B'$ the base change, $b'\in B'$ and $\Omega$ an algebraic closure of $\kappa(b')$. By associativity of sheaf fibre products, $H'\times_{B'}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega=H\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ for the composite $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to B'\to B$, whose image is $h(b')$. By the previous paragraph this geometric fibre is nonempty and pure of dimension $d(h(b'))$, so $d_{p_{B'}}(b')=d_p(h(b'))$. No flatness of $h$ is used, and no property of $p'$ beyond this identification of its geometric fibres.

lean.note: All geometric fibres after every scheme base change are characterized by one locally constant function on the original base. The identity base change gives the original fibres; associativity of sheaf fibre products identifies the arbitrary-base-change fibres, so their dimension function is d composed with the base map. The group-valued functor retains noncommutative multiplication, inverse and identity. The added landed dependency supplies the shared MapToSchemeIsLocally, MapToSchemeIsSeparated and MapIsQuasiCompact predicates. groupGeometricFibre is an explicit canonical presheaf pullback, without any chosen data.
